subject: SCCs: runtime operator escrow, in-region keystore handling & deletion SLA
messages:
From: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@medicorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: data-privacy@medicorp.com, legal@medicorp.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Runtime operator escrow + SCCs questions

Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. During our internal risk review a couple of specific operational questions came up that are blockers for final procurement sign-off. Can you confirm the following for EU-only processing under SCCs?

1) Operator escrow / break-glass: we need a description of what operational access your operators can have to in-region inference instances, who holds the escalation keys, and whether Redwood supports an escrow/third-party custodian model for those keys.

2) Keystore/location of KMS-protected model artifacts and KV cache: does any model or cache material replicate out of the EU under normal operation or failover?

3) Deletion SLA and proof: we require an auditable runbook for customer-initiated deletion requests (including backups and snapshot retention) and an estimated RTO for full erasure.

If you can send a short attestation and any artifacts (network map, key custody statement, deletion runbook) we can advance legal review.

I can be flexible on format — PDF or CSV for mappings is fine.

Ivan
Head of Platform Security
Medicorp

---

Subject: Re: Runtime operator escrow + SCCs questions

Ivan — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Irene (infrastructure/security) and Lauren (legal/evidence) to provide the attestation and artifacts.

Quick answers for context while they pull docs:
- Operator access: Operators have role-based runbook access for emergency actions only; we support an escrow model with a neutral custodian for escalation keys (we typically propose Charlton Trust as the custodian).
- KMS/keystore: Production key material for customer in-region deployments is managed by the customer's KMS (we provide integrations with major cloud KMS or on-prem HSM); ephemeral runtime caches do not replicate outside the region under normal operation.
- Deletion: We provide a documented runbook and an auditable deletion ticket that includes snapshots, backups, and KV cache invalidation. Typical full erasure RTO for EU-only deployments is 72 hours for primary stores and up to 14 days for cold backups depending on retention/legal holds.

Irene — can you attach the in-region operator map, the SCCS appendix, and the deletion runbook (redwood-sccs-appendix.pdf, inregion-operator-map.csv, deletion-runbook-v1.docx)?

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Attestation + artifacts for EU-only SCCs requests

Ivan — attaching the artifacts requested and a short attestation below. Attachments: redwood-sccs-appendix.pdf, inregion-operator-map.csv, deletion-runbook-v1.docx (see attached stubs).

Attestation (high level):
- Scope: This attestation covers Redwood Inference EU-only processing deployments (single-tenant VPC and dedicated clusters provisioned in EU regions) when customer requests exclusive processing under our SCCs-based contract addendum.
- Operator access: Operators are limited to named support engineers; emergency break-glass access requires multi-party approval and is cryptographically gated. Redwood offers an escrow option with third-party custodian (Charlton Trust) where the custodian retains the split key shares; Redwood cannot unilaterally reconstruct the key without custodian approval.
- KMS and artifact residency: Customer-managed KMS is the default for production deployments. Model artifacts and persistent KV caches for EU-only customers are stored on region-local storage and do not replicate across borders in normal operation. Failover within EU regions is supported; cross-border replication to non-EU regions is only performed if explicitly authorized in writing by the customer.
- Deletion and evidence: Deletion requests are processed via our deletion-runbook-v1.docx. Primary data erasure for active stores: target 72 hours. Cold backups and long-term snapshots are scheduled for deletion within 14 days unless under legal hold. All deletion actions create an auditable ticket (including snapshot ids, operator ids, and signed deletion receipts) which can be exported for third-party audit.

We can provide a redacted sample deletion ticket and an operator-access ledger export under an NDA if Medicorp wants more granular evidence.

Next steps:
- Lauren: can your team confirm whether the escrow custodian proposal is acceptable to Medicorp legal and whether you want a sample custodian agreement?
- Naomi: please prepare a redacted deletion ticket and the ledger export sample.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
